chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Qummī, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq, the nephew of Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Five are to be waited upon unless they change: the drowned person, the one struck down, the one suffering from abdominal affliction, the one buried under a collapse, and the smoke-stricken.”

key_terms.الْمَبْطُونُ: the person afflicted by a severe abdominal illness
key_terms.الْمَصْعُوقُ: the person struck down or rendered unconscious by a violent shock
key_terms.الْمَهْدُومُ: the person trapped or crushed under a collapsed structure
key_terms.يَتَغَيَّرُوا: they show bodily change indicating confirmed death
key_terms.يُنْتَظَرُ: they are to be waited on before acting definitively

ai.seo_question: Which types of apparently deceased persons should be waited on before funeral rites are performed?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal precaution concerning five categories of those thought to have died: they should not be treated immediately as dead, unless signs of bodily change appear. Its significance lies in funeral jurisprudence and the care required before proceeding with rites for those whose death may not yet be certain.
